metadata.note: P vs θ graph from Table 1 is perfectly linear; extrapolated to P=0, it crosses θ-axis at −273°C. Marks: 1m for stating/reading −273°C (or −270 to −275°C range), 1m for naming it 'absolute zero', 1m for recognising this implies P∝T (Kelvin). Follows Q1b(i) (graph plotting — not auto-gradeable).

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q1b(ii) — Extrapolate Graph to Find Absolute Zero
question.text:
Extrapolate (extend) the best-fit line on the pressure–temperature (P vs θ) graph until it meets the temperature axis. Mark this point X on your graph.

(ii) State:

  • The temperature value at point X
  • The name given to this temperature value

(3 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Extrapolation result:
The P vs θ graph, when extrapolated to P = 0, crosses the temperature axis at θ = −273 °C.

Name: This temperature is called absolute zero — the lowest theoretically possible temperature, at which all particle motion effectively ceases and gas pressure would reach zero.

In SI units, absolute zero = 0 K (Kelvin). The Kelvin scale starts at absolute zero: T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.
